questions.q: What technology does a restaurant need?
questions.a: Most restaurants start with a POS system, then add online ordering, a kitchen display system, inventory software and reservations as they grow. Guest experience, loyalty, payments, back-office and staff scheduling tools round out the stack. You don't need everything at once, so begin with the areas that cost you the most time or money.

questions.q: Why is the POS system so important for a restaurant?
questions.a: Your POS is where every sale is recorded, so it becomes the central source of data for the whole business. Beyond taking payments, it feeds menu engineering, labor planning, cash control and financial reporting. Choosing one that connects well with your other tools makes the rest of your stack far easier to run.

questions.q: Are third-party delivery apps worth it for restaurants?
questions.a: They can widen your reach beyond the neighborhood, but you should weigh their fees and commissions against your margins. These apps also hold most of the customer data, so you usually don't get full access to who your guests are. Bringing feedback from delivery platforms into one place helps you keep sight of how those guests feel.

questions.q: How does technology help manage a restaurant's reputation?
questions.a: Reputation tools track what guests say across review sites and social media and help you reply quickly and consistently. Momos, for example, brings reviews, surveys and social feedback into one Unified Inbox, where AI drafts on-brand replies and analytics show what drives positive and negative reviews. That lets you fix issues before they spread across locations.

questions.q: How should I roll out new technology in my restaurant?
questions.a: Start with your biggest bottleneck, such as slow ticket times, labor waste or few repeat guests, and fix that first. Choose tools built for restaurants, since they already account for how restaurants operate. Make sure your POS, ordering, kitchen, loyalty and accounting systems connect so your team isn't entering the same data twice.
